answer: Treat trust like an orchard: a new agent only bears fruit after three established agents vouch for it, and each voucher locks part of its own stake behind that vouch. If the newcomer is later exposed as a sybil, the vouchers lose that bond. No agent is a safe haven for fakes, because propping up a knoll of sock puppets means risking real stake per fake identity, so a cheap army quickly becomes an expensive one.
